name: DLP Policies Cover Exchange and SharePoint/OneDrive

impactRating.rationale: Failure to apply DLP policies across Exchange and SharePoint exposes the tenant to: Undetected exfiltration of regulated data (PII, financial records, health information) via email attachments and file sharing without policy enforcement.

Failure to configure auto-sensitivity labeling policies exposes the tenant to: Sensitive data stored without classification labels, bypassing DLP controls and encryption policies that depend on label presence for enforcement.

Failure to enable communication compliance monitoring exposes the tenant to: Regulatory violations, insider trading activity, and hostile workplace communications going undetected without policy-based surveillance of internal messaging.

name: Ensure MX records exist and point to Exchange Online for all email domains

impactRating.rationale: Failure to route email through Exchange Online mail flow exposes the tenant to: Security control bypass; mail not traversing Exchange Online skips ATP scanning, DLP policies, mail flow rules, and anti-phishing defenses.
Informational: surfaces the total count of disabled member accounts alongside total directory size. High ratios may indicate accounts pending removal or an offboarding gap.

name: Ensure that 'Users can create Microsoft 365 groups in Azure portals, API or PowerShell' is set to 'No'

impactRating.rationale: Unrestricted Microsoft 365 group creation leads to group sprawl, unmanaged Teams and SharePoint sites, and ungoverned external sharing locations.

name: Ensure password addition is blocked for applications

impactRating.rationale: Client secrets are long-lived, easily leaked credentials. Blocking new password credentials tenant-wide forces certificate or federated credentials for applications and service principals.

name: Ensure password lifetime for applications does not exceed 180 days

impactRating.rationale: Long-lived application secrets extend the window in which a leaked credential can be abused. A tenant-wide maximum lifetime bounds that exposure.

name: Ensure new application passwords are system-generated

impactRating.rationale: Custom, user-chosen application secrets are often weak or reused. Requiring system-generated secrets guarantees sufficient entropy.

name: Ensure maximum certificate lifetime for applications does not exceed 180 days

impactRating.rationale: Long-lived application certificates extend the exposure window of a stolen private key. A tenant-wide maximum lifetime bounds that exposure.

name: Ensure that periodic reauthentication is required for all users

impactRating.rationale: Without a sign-in frequency ceiling, stolen or long-lived sessions and refresh tokens remain usable indefinitely. Periodic reauthentication limits session replay.

name: Ensure trusted named locations are defined

impactRating.rationale: Location-aware Conditional Access policies depend on trusted named locations being defined and maintained.

name: Ensure exclusionary geographic access controls are utilized

impactRating.rationale: Blocking sign-ins from locations the organization never operates in removes a large share of opportunistic credential-attack traffic.

name: Ensure Token Protection is enforced for session tokens

impactRating.rationale: Token protection cryptographically binds sign-in tokens to the device, defeating token theft and replay for Exchange Online, SharePoint Online and Teams on Windows.
Authentication transfer lets a session on one device be handed to another, bypassing device-bound controls. Blocking it closes that path.

name: Ensure that Account 'Lockout duration in seconds' is at least 60 seconds

impactRating.rationale: A very short smart-lockout duration lets password-guessing resume almost immediately, weakening protection against brute force and password spray.

name: Ensure Microsoft Authenticator on companion applications is disabled

impactRating.rationale: Allowing Authenticator approvals inside companion applications places an MFA factor in the same context as the resource being protected, weakening phishing and fatigue resistance.

name: Ensure the ability to add personal email accounts and calendars is disabled

impactRating.rationale: Connecting personal accounts in Outlook on the web creates an unmonitored path for corporate data to leave via consumer mailboxes.

name: Ensure DLP policies are published for Copilot users

impactRating.rationale: Without DLP coverage of Microsoft 365 Copilot interactions, sensitive data can be surfaced or shared through prompts and responses outside normal controls.
